cues.en: Now in the previous lecture, we have created a new method and we have inserted new elements to this
cube.
Now in this lecture we are going to look at the cube method.
Now the cube method means that it's removing the elements from the cube.
But here take into account that we cannot remove any element from the end of the cube or middle of the
cube.
So we have to remove the elements from the beginning of the cube.
Now, if you want to remove the element from the beginning of the array, in this case, we are just
going to use the shift method of the array.
Now whenever we are calling the dequeue method, it's going to remove the element from the beginning
of the cube.
So in this case the first element in the queue is ten.
Then all other elements will be moved to the place of the first element.
So it's going to shift one step left.
Then if we call it one more time, one more time, the elements will be shifted one step left over here
in the array.
So the next element becomes the first element in the cube.
Now that's how the dequeue method works.
So as I mentioned before, this is going to be the very simplest form of the dequeue method.
If you want to return any specific message after performing this operation, you can put it as a return
statement.
So here after enqueue method, I will declare a new method which is going to be the dequeue.
So we have mentioned that it's not going to take any parameter.
Then here all we have to do is we're just going to call shift method.
Now if I just go ahead and call the dequeue method for this queue.
So I'll just put over here the queue.
So the first element that we have inserted was ten.
So it's going to remove the ten from the queue.
So I'll just clear the console and run this.
When we print out the new queue we will have only two elements over here.
So as you can see ten is removed from here.
Now we can just go ahead and return it from this dequeue method.
Now I'll just clear the console and run this.
You will see that in this case it is returning ten.
So that's how the dequeue method works.
So it's obvious that the time complexity for this method is going to be o n.
Because whenever we are dequeuing the element from the beginning of the array, all elements has to
shift one step left.
That's why the time complexity for this is going to be n and the space complexity is O one, because
here an additional memory is not required to perform this operations.
That's why the space complexity is O one.
